verses.text: I wish you were like a brother to me, someone who nursed at my mother's breasts. If I met you outside, I could kiss you and nobody would look down on me.
I'd lead you to my mother's house, where she could teach me. I'd give you spiced wine to drink, juice from my own pomegranate.
His left hand would cradle my head, and his right arm would wrap around me.
Daughters of Jerusalem, promise me this. Don't stir up love or wake it before it wants to wake.
Who's this coming up from the wilderness, leaning on her love? Beloved: I woke you under the apple tree. That's where your mother conceived you, where she went into labor and gave birth to you.
Set me like a seal on your heart, like a seal on your arm. Love is strong as death, and jealousy is as cruel as the grave. Its sparks are sparks of fire, a flame of the LORD himself.
All the water in the world can't put love out, and floods can't drown it. If someone offered every bit of their family's wealth for love, people would laugh them to scorn.
We have a little sister whose breasts haven't grown yet. What will we do for her when someone comes asking to marry her?
If she's a wall, we'll build a silver turret on her. If she's a door, we'll close her in with cedar boards.
I'm a wall, and my breasts are like towers. That's how I became someone who found peace in his eyes.
Solomon had a vineyard at Baal Hamon. He rented it out to caretakers. Each one was to bring a thousand shekels of silver for its fruit.
My own vineyard is mine to decide about. You can have the thousand, Solomon, and two hundred go to the people who tend the fruit.
You who live in the gardens, with friends listening in, let me hear your voice!
Come away, my love! Be like a gazelle or a young stag out on the mountains of spices!
